title: Last night's backup never reached the NAS

lines.text: 07:10 NAS report: no backup received from office1 last night
08:00 NAS: off-site replication ran without office1's backup
NAS report: backup received from office1

meters.label: Minutes spent paging the unfiltered journal

objective: Read service logs with journalctl filtered by unit, boot, priority and time
secondaryObjectives: Mount filesystems by hand and at boot through /etc/fstab using UUIDs
Troubleshoot a service that fails to start from its status and journal

sources.note: Relevant text: -b, 'The argument may be empty, in which case logs for the current boot will be shown' (-1 selects the boot before); -p, 'If a single log level is specified, all messages with this log level or a lower' numeric value, that is more important, are shown; -u, 'Show messages for the specified systemd unit'; -S/--since, 'the strings "yesterday", "today", "tomorrow" are understood'; --list-boots, 'Show a tabular list of boot numbers (relative to the current boot), their IDs' and first and last message times. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: 'The previous contents (if any) and owner and mode of dir become invisible, and as long as this filesystem remains mounted, the pathname dir refers to the root of the filesystem on device.' So with nothing mounted, /mnt/backup is an ordinary directory on the root filesystem. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. The CIFS 'mount error(13): Permission denied' line is authored in mount.cifs's style.

Relevant text: RequiresMountsFor= 'Takes a space-separated list of absolute paths. Automatically adds dependencies of type Requires= and After= for all mount units required to access the specified path.' Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. Used in the debrief as the follow-up, not as an action.

brief.situation: You look after office1, the file server at Pembrook and Shah Accounting (fictional). A systemd timer runs backup.service at 01:30, which copies client files to //nas1/backup mounted at /mnt/backup. The NAS reports nothing arrived last night. The NAS copies everything off-site at 08:00, and a backup takes about 20 minutes. office1 also rebooted for updates at 02:00.
handover: The NAS administrator changed the backup account's password yesterday at 17:00; the new one is in the password manager.
/mnt/backup is mounted from /etc/fstab with the credentials file /etc/backup-nas.cred.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments are fixed.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, disk or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: How many operator minutes each command takes, and when the fictional outage spreads, are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values. Off-site replication runs at 08:00, 50 minutes after the start.

writeup.question: For the record: why last night's backup failed, which journalctl filters found it, and what stops it failing silently next time.

parts.label: Cause
parts.criteria: Names the NAS refusing the mount at 01:30 after yesterday's password change, and the backup script refusing to run on an unmounted path.
parts.modelAnswer: The password changed at 17:00; at 01:30 mount.cifs got Permission denied, and backup.sh exited 1 because /mnt/backup was not mounted.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Uses a filter that reaches the previous boot or the unit since yesterday (-b -1, -u with --since), not the current boot's errors or the whole journal.
parts.modelAnswer: The 02:00 reboot put 01:30 in boot -1: journalctl -b -1 -p err, or -u backup.service -u mnt-backup.mount --since yesterday, showed the mount error and the refusal.

parts.label: Fix and follow-up
parts.criteria: Updates the credentials, mounts, runs the backup job before 08:00 and checks the mount; never writes the backup into the unmounted directory; suggests RequiresMountsFor= or an alert on failure.
parts.modelAnswer: New password in /etc/backup-nas.cred, mount /mnt/backup, systemctl start backup.service (done 07:3x), df shows //nas1 on /mnt/backup. Follow-up: RequiresMountsFor=/mnt/backup and an OnFailure= alert.

expertPath.text: The 02:00 reboot means 01:30 is in boot -1: journalctl -b -1 -p err, or the two units --since yesterday.
mount error(13) at 01:30 and 'not mounted; refusing to run': yesterday's password change.
Put the new password in /etc/backup-nas.cred and mount /mnt/backup.
systemctl start backup.service (about 20 minutes), df to confirm the NAS is under /mnt/backup; propose RequiresMountsFor= and a failure alert.

fixed.headline: Good: found fast, backed up in time
fixed.body: You reached for the previous boot and the right units, read the actual error, and got the backup to the NAS before it went off-site.

fixedGaps.headline: Backed up, with gaps
fixedGaps.body: The backup is on the NAS. The criteria show what it cost: minutes paging, or a fix before the evidence that pushed it past 08:00.

rootFilled.headline: The server's own disk filled
rootFilled.body: With nothing mounted, /mnt/backup is just a directory on /. The backup script refused for exactly that reason; a manual rsync did not.

noBackup.headline: Closed with no backup
noBackup.body: journalctl -b alone shows only this boot. The backup ran before the 02:00 reboot, so ask for -b -1 or a unit with --since.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The machine rebooted after the backup's run, so this boot's journal cannot show it: filter the previous boot (-b -1 -p err) or the units with --since yesterday. The mount was refused after the password change and the script refused to write to an unmounted path. Fix the credentials, mount, run the job, and check with df; never copy into the bare directory.
